title: Ephraim Mikshaa
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was Rabbi Meir’s disciple and spoke in his name: [Bava Metzia 87a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.87a.6), [Sanhedrin 39b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.39b.15), and [Bereshit Rabbah 48:14](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.48.14) and [85:10](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.85.10). Hyman cites Rashi for the explanation that he guarded cucumbers; at the end of Tosefta Shabbat, cucumbers are called mikshaot. Others explain the epithet as one who poses difficult halakhic questions.[^1]

notes.text: All four passages name Ephraim as Rabbi Meir’s student and transmitter. The [commentary attributed to Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Bereshit_Rabbah.85.10.2) gives both interpretations of the epithet. [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=636&lang=en) records the two explanations from Mattanot Kehunnah and a third, “cucumber seller,” from Yedei Moshe.
